# Benchmark report (auto-generated by `scripts/evaluate.py` - do not edit by hand)

> **DATA WARNING.** Data source(s): **SYNTHETIC**. If this says SYNTHETIC, every number below measures how
> well the models recover the *synthetic generator's* dynamics. These are **not clinical results** and say nothing about real patients,
> and nothing about type 2 vs type 1 diabetes in any real population.

## Design
- Data MD5 (of uncompressed readings) `2a4bb446604a39157250b007e55b3928`, seed 2026, model version `glucotwin-lgbm-cgm_tod-b09655ec` (primary variant: `cgm_tod` - CGM features + local time of day).
- Patient-disjoint split: {'train': 60, 'val_select': 10, 'val_calibrate': 10, 'test': 20}. Test patients: 20 (demo patients SYNTH-001..003 are among them). Excluded in test: none.
- Input window 60 min (5 readings @ 15 min); horizons 15-120 min; first 48 h of every patient is calibration-only and never scored.
- Test origins: 23,040 grid slots, 22,242 with a reading, 20,825 with a complete input window (forecast issued).
- Primary variant chosen on `val_select` patients only (parsimony rule, `experiments/model_selection.json`); intervals calibrated on `val_calibrate` patients; the test patients were not used for any choice.
- All models are scored on **identical cases** per horizon (asserted in code).

## 3. Patient-level results
Primary model has lower mean MAE than persistence for **20 of 20** test patients. Per-patient table is in `experiments/results.json`.

Per-patient mean coverage: min 0.710, median 0.798, max 0.855;
0 of 20 patients are more than 10 points below nominal. Interval width is constant per horizon (split-conformal, non-adaptive), so mean and median widths coincide. Conformal guarantees are *marginal* (averaged over patients), not per-patient.

## 5. Abstention and input quality
- Grid slots without any reading: 798 of 23,040.
- Observed origins where the forecast was **withheld** (incomplete 60-min window, no imputation): 1,417 of 22,242 (**6.4%**).
- Forecasts issued but **qualified** as out-of-distribution: 233 (1.12%).
- Mean MAE in-distribution 16.09 mg/dL; out-of-distribution 14.34 mg/dL.
- The missingness rate is a parameter of the synthetic generator, not a measured property of any real device.

## 6. Event task: new hyperglycaemia onset (research label, not an alarm)
event = latest glucose <= 180 mg/dL AND true glucose exceeds 180 mg/dL at any of the next 8 readings (15-120 min). Test origins eligible: 15,189; events: 3,913 (base rate 25.8%).
Decision offset for each learned model was tuned on `val_select` only.

| Model | TP | FP | FN | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| persistence | 0 | 0 | 3913 | n/a (no positive predictions) | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| ridge_cgm | 2930 | 6642 | 983 | 0.306 | 0.749 | 0.435 |
| lgbm_cgm_tod | 3094 | 1991 | 819 | 0.608 | 0.791 | 0.688 |

Persistence can never predict a threshold crossing from a value at or below the threshold, so its recall is 0 by construction.

## 7. Failure analysis (primary, 120-min horizon)
- MAE by trend phase: {"rising_>30mgdl_per_h": 12.1, "falling_<-30": 17.2, "flat_|slope|<=30": 22.6}
- Worst five forecasts (patient / origin UTC / latest / true +120 / predicted +120): SYNTH-029 2026-01-18 13:15 248/396/168; SYNTH-029 2026-01-11 06:00 131/400/175; SYNTH-048 2026-01-13 07:45 139/400/188; SYNTH-048 2026-01-11 14:30 141/395/184; SYNTH-048 2026-01-13 08:00 141/388/182
- Meals are unobserved by the model, so excursions that start after the forecast origin cannot be anticipated except through learned schedule regularities.

## Limitations
Synthetic data only in this report; one 14-day record per patient; fixed hyper-parameters; single random seed for the split; no clinical validation; type 2 population claims are not supported.
